landmarks.method: Exit point of the facial-nerve centreline from the temporal-bone volume (last inside node before it leaves for good), snapped to the bone surface.
Sharpest turn (first genu) of the facial-nerve centreline within 8 mm after it passes the cochlea.
First facial-nerve centreline node inside the bone that comes within 2.5 mm of the cochlea (start of the labyrinthine part). The model does not hollow out the meatus, so this is an estimate.

landmarks.n: Internal acoustic opening (porus of internal acoustic meatus)
landmarks.method: Where the CN VII centreline (and, independently, the CN VIII centreline) first reaches the temporal bone (≤ 0.8 mm or inside); mean of both, snapped to the surface.
First node of the internal-carotid centreline (from the neck upwards) that lies inside or ≤ 2.5 mm from the temporal bone (artery in the canal lumen), snapped to the surface.
Last node of the internal-carotid centreline that is inside or ≤ 2.5 mm from the temporal bone (where the artery leaves the petrous apex), snapped to the surface.
Mean of the points where the CN IX, X and XI centreline pass closest to BOTH the temporal and the occipital bone (minimising the larger of the two distances).
Point outside bone within 15 mm of the petrous apex that is closest to all three of temporal, sphenoid and occipital bone (1 mm grid). The cartilage-filled gap is approximated, not modelled.
Temporal-bone surface point closest to the centre of the TMJ articular disc.
Lowest temporal-bone surface point 3–20 mm anterior to the mandibular fossa within ±8 mm of its lateral position (the eminence in front of the fossa).
Mandible surface point closest to the centre of the TMJ articular disc.
Temporal-bone point closest to the zygomatic bone (the temporozygomatic suture at the tip of the zygomatic process).

landmarks.n: External acoustic meatus (medial end, tympanic membrane)
landmarks.method: Centre of the tympanic-membrane mesh, which closes the medial end of the external acoustic meatus. The lateral opening (porus acusticus externus) is not derivable and is on the pin list.
Where the inferior-alveolar-nerve centreline (from above) enters the mandible, snapped to the surface.
Highest mandible point within 4 mm of the temporalis insertion patch (the temporalis inserts on the coronoid process).
Most posterior-inferior mandible point on this side (maximises posterior minus superior position).
Lowest point of the upper border of the ramus between the coronoid tip and the condylar head (top surface per 1 mm anteroposterior bin, then its minimum).
Centre of the first (lowest) run of vertebral-artery centreline nodes inside or ≤ 1.5 mm from the Axis (C2).
Centre of the first (lowest) run of vertebral-artery centreline nodes inside or ≤ 1.5 mm from the Atlas (C1).
Most lateral point of the atlas on this side.
